newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Steady amid lack of direction.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Steady amid lack of direction.

text.p: Light distillates were steady on Monday as the market was stymied awaiting firmer direction, traders said.
The market was awaiting direction from Taiwan's and India's gasoline purchase tenders, both of which close on June 4, to provide some direction, they said.
"Other than Taiwan and India, there is no demand," a trader said.
Taiwan seeks 95-octane unleaded reformate for second-half July delivery while India requires 87-octane with a lead content of 0.15 grammes per litre, for June 18-22 delivery.
India's requirements to Bombay on the Indian west coast are likely to be sourced from the Mideast, traders said.
In the Singapore fob market, only a Dutch trader offered the 92-octane at $23.70 per barrel for June 26-30 lifting.
The grade was offered on Friday at $23.80 lifting June 22-26 and was last traded on Wednesday at $23.75 for June 15-20 lifting.
Naphtha was steady with June swaps marginally lower at $21.80/$22.10 per barrel from $21.85/$22.10 on Friday.
July swaps were around 10 cents in contango due to high stocks and weak reegional demand.
Traders said a U.S. major has sold 120-140,000-barrels of light naphtha lifting end-June/early July fob Singapore but details were confidential.
But they assessed premiums at 40-70 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes, fob.
